specId.fullTitle: Defect Management Using BCF - Use case

authoring.copyright: Copyright 2026 Building Informatics Group (BIG), Yonsei University. Tutorial sample; fictitious project data; not normative.

description.title: The general contractor identifies construction defects on site, logs each defect as a BIM Collaboration Format (BCF) topic linked to the building model, triages and assigns it to the responsible trade subcontractor, verifies the rectification and closes the topic. A daily defect status report summarises the BCF topics for the owner's representative.
Aim: replace paper punch lists and spreadsheet defect logs with BCF topics that carry location, photographs, status and responsibility, so that every party works on the same defect record.

businessRule.name: Unique defect identification
businessRule.statement: Every defect shall have a globally unique identifier and a project defect number that is never reused.

description.title: Commentary: the BCF topic GUID is the unique identifier; the defect number (e.g. DEF-0001) is the server-assigned id of the topic.

businessRule.name: Defect location
businessRule.statement: Every defect shall be located by storey and space and, where it affects a modelled element, by the IFC GlobalId of that element.

description.title: Commentary: the element is referenced as a selected component in the viewpoint of the BCF topic.

businessRule.name: Photographic evidence
businessRule.statement: Every defect found in an inspection shall include at least one photograph of the defect, carried as the snapshot of the first viewpoint of the BCF topic.

businessRule.name: Controlled vocabularies
businessRule.statement: The topic type, topic status, priority, labels and users of a defect shall be values defined in the project BCF extensions (extensions.xml).

description.title: Commentary: topic type = Defect; statuses = Open, Assigned, In progress, Resolved, Reopened, Closed, Rejected; priorities = P1 - Critical, P2 - High, P3 - Medium, P4 - Low.

businessRule.name: Defect status lifecycle
businessRule.statement: The status of a defect shall change only along the transitions of the defect status lifecycle.

description.title: Commentary: a defect can be closed only from Resolved, and a Reopened defect returns to Assigned.

businessRule.name: Triage deadline
businessRule.statement: A logged defect shall be triaged within 2 working days of its creation date.
businessRule.reference: Project quality plan, clause 7.3 Defect management (illustrative)

businessRule.name: Rectification period by priority
businessRule.statement: The due date of a defect shall be no later than 1 day (P1 - Critical), 7 days (P2 - High), 14 days (P3 - Medium) or 30 days (P4 - Low) after triage.
businessRule.reference: Project quality plan, clause 7.4 Response times (illustrative)

businessRule.name: Safety-critical defects
businessRule.statement: A defect that is flagged as safety-critical shall have the priority P1 - Critical.

description.title: Commentary: the area shall also be made safe immediately; this is a site instruction and is not checked from the data.

businessRule.reference: Occupational Safety and Health Act (Republic of Korea) (illustrative)

businessRule.name: Single responsible assignee
businessRule.statement: An assigned defect shall have exactly one assignee, who is a registered project user of the responsible party.

businessRule.name: Evidence of rectification
businessRule.statement: A defect shall be set to Resolved only with a rectification description and at least one photograph taken after rectification.

businessRule.name: Independent verification
businessRule.statement: The person who verifies a rectification shall not be the assignee of the defect.

description.title: Commentary: segregation of duties; the verifier is normally the site quality inspector.

businessRule.reference: ISO 9001:2015, 8.6 Release of products and services

businessRule.name: Closure after passed verification
businessRule.statement: A defect shall be closed only after a verification with the result Passed; a rejected defect shall record the reason for rejection.

businessRule.name: Escalation of repeated failures
businessRule.statement: A defect whose rectification fails verification more than twice shall be escalated to the project manager.

businessRule.name: Daily defect status report
businessRule.statement: A defect status report shall be issued every working day with the number of defects by status, priority and trade, the list of overdue defects and the average time to close.

description.title: One defect record from identification to closure; defects located in the model; measurable response times; fewer disputes about responsibility.
BCF does not define defect-specific fields such as severity or root cause; they are carried as labels or comments by project convention (see the BCF extensions of the project).
BCF 3.0 capable issue management tool or common data environment (CDE); IFC 4.3 coordination model; mobile device with camera for site inspection.
Site inspection and quality control; use of a BCF viewer; knowledge of the project quality plan.

description.title: working_days(IU-LOG-017, IU-TRI-071) <= 2

import numpy as np

description.title: IU-ASG-04 - IU-TRI-071 <= 1 d (P1), 7 d (P2), 14 d (P3), 30 d (P4) according to IU-TRI-03

constraint.expression: PREFIX bcf: <https://example.org/bcf#> PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> ASK { # true = violation ?t a bcf:Topic ; bcf:topicType "Defect" ; bcf:priority ?p ; bcf:dueDate ?due ; bcf:triagedOn ?tri . VALUES (?p ?days) { ("P1 - Critical" 1) ("P2 - High" 7) ("P3 - Medium" 14) ("P4 - Low" 30) } FILTER ( (xsd:date(?due) - xsd:date(?tri)) > xsd:dayTimeDuration(CONCAT("P", STR(?days), "D")) ) }
